cues: Phenol is a colourless solid that forms long needle shaped crystals, melting at forty one degrees and boiling at one eighty two.
Left in air and light it slowly turns pink.
It has a sharp carbolic smell, and it is corrosive, raising painful blisters on skin.
It dissolves only a little in cold water, about eight grams per hundred, but mixes completely above sixty six degrees.
Like alcohols, its molecules are linked by hydrogen bonds, which explains its high boiling point.
